Mediocre like any other app
I had high hopes for Simply Piano because I purchased it for my daughter and she consistently practiced and put a lot of effort into it. Unfortunately, after using it for a while, I became very frustrated with the experience.

The lessons feel repetitive and seem more focused on keeping you using the app rather than actually teaching you how to play the piano independently. My biggest issue is that you become completely reliant on the app. I was hoping for a program that would genuinely teach my daughter the fundamentals, so that over time she could sit at the piano and actually play without needing the app guiding her through everything.

For the price, I expected much more depth and progression. I can understand why many people become frustrated after realizing that practicing with the app doesn’t necessarily translate into being able to confidently play on your own.

What made the experience even worse was the subscription renewal. I requested a refund the day after my trial ended, but Apple repeatedly rejected my refund request. I wasn’t trying to continue the subscription and immediately asked for the charge to be reversed. Being charged $249 for something I no longer wanted, and then having the refund denied, was extremely disappointing.

Overall, I feel the product is overpriced for what it offers, and the subscription model makes the experience even more frustrating. I would not recommend it, especially at this price.

Unfortunately, a few months in my review is mostly negative
It seems like it is becoming less enjoyable by the day.  Here’s some features in particular that take the shine off the product:

1.  The scrolling music approach is fine, unless you come to a difficult passage.  The program has a tendency to always be pushing you, which can be quite annoying, and if you screw up a couple of times, it changes to metronome mode which is generally infuriating.  If you pause the scrolling to practice a passage, you don’t generally have enough time to get your hands back on the keyboard when you restart the scrolling,  resulting in errors and entry into that annoying metronome mode.  What would be much better, would be a manual / non-scrolling practice mode that allows you to move the score back and forth by swiping it with your finger.  This would be more like the traditional way of practicing a new piece of sheet music.  After practicing in this manner, you could jump back into the auto-scrolling (push-push-push) mode of operation.

2.  In this scrolling music approach, it shows very little of the score at a time, just a few bars, which makes it more difficult to play harder pieces.  I gather this is because some people are trying to use the app on their phone, which seems crazy to me.  You would end up with terrible posture and eye strain if you did this for very long.

3.  The program has a tendency to push you along through the practice segments even if you are screwing up the tempo and the notes pretty badly.  This simply (no pun intended) results in bad timing, and poor mastery of sight reading.  Eventually, you hit a wall. That’s where I have been for several weeks and it’s both discouraging, and making it mentally difficult to look forward to practice.

4.  During the learning segments, it regularly incorporates odd rhythmic accompaniment.  For instance, jazz or rock accompaniment for a classical score.  Half the time, you can’t even discern the time signature / beat of this odd accompaniment.  It simply leads to bad timing skills.  I’d much rather have just a simple metronome beat for accompaniment, unless it is playing the actual accompaniment for the piece.

5.  What little sheet music that is provided with the application, can only be viewed in landscape mode.  Thus, you can only see a couple of lines at a time when viewing these sheet music selections.

App problems, poor support and £114 refund outstanding
I experienced persistent problems with Simply Piano over several months. Despite repeated complaints, the issues were never satisfactorily resolved.

In September, the company agreed to refund £114. When repayment difficulties arose, I accepted their offer of an Amazon voucher instead. Weeks later, I have received neither.

Customer support has been extremely disappointing, with repetitive automated responses that ignore the history of my complaint. Most recently, I was told refunds take 24–48 hours, despite having waited weeks.

I cannot recommend a subscription service that handles legitimate complaints in this way. I would welcome Simply Piano finally honouring its promise.

Expensive, but worth it
Expensive, but worth it.

The free test phase is really short and they charge you very fast. So beware!

But if you seriously want to start to play piano the app is really great! The structure is profound and you learn step by step in a thoughtful way.

The biggest strength is that you get motivated to practice. And I think to learn piano is all about practice. The continuous feedback is very helpful.

Try it if you serious about learning piano, so its an investment.
